title: Opposite injective-simplex inclusion preserves cocone spaces
statement:
Use small simplicial sets, standard simplices, ordinary nerves, quasicategories, functor simplicial sets, constant diagrams and right-pinched Kan mapping spaces of [def-cbc-enhanced-diagrams-cones], with universes enlarged as necessary. For a small simplicial set $X$, let $\mathsf S(X)$ be the ordinary category whose objects are all simplices $\sigma:\Delta^n\to X$, including degenerate simplices, and whose morphisms $\sigma\to\tau$ are monotone maps $\alpha:[n]\to[m]$ with $\tau\Delta(\alpha)=\sigma$; composition is composition of the monotone maps. Let $\mathsf S_{\mathrm{inj}}(X)\subseteq\mathsf S(X)$ have all the same objects and only those morphisms for which $\alpha$ is injective; its objects still include degenerate simplices of $X$. Let
$$j_X:N(\mathsf S_{\mathrm{inj}}(X)^{\mathrm{op}})\longrightarrow N(\mathsf S(X)^{\mathrm{op}})$$
be induced by inclusion. For every quasicategory $\mathcal E$, every map $p:N(\mathsf S(X)^{\mathrm{op}})\to\mathcal E$ and every vertex $T\in\mathcal E$, restriction itself induces an equivalence of Kan complexes
$$\operatorname{Map}_{\operatorname{Fun}(N(\mathsf S(X)^{\mathrm{op}}),\mathcal E)}(p,\Delta_{N(\mathsf S(X)^{\mathrm{op}})}T)\longrightarrow\operatorname{Map}_{\operatorname{Fun}(N(\mathsf S_{\mathrm{inj}}(X)^{\mathrm{op}}),\mathcal E)}(pj_X,\Delta_{N(\mathsf S_{\mathrm{inj}}(X)^{\mathrm{op}})}T).$$
No quasicategory hypothesis on $X$ or colimit-existence hypothesis on $\mathcal E$ is imposed; the empty case is included.

mathlib_searches.query: Inclusion of injective simplex operators into all simplex operators, with categories opposite, is cofinal for any simplicial set
mathlib_searches.results: Eight hits: stdSimplex.faceRepresentableBy, SSet.N.le_iff_exists_mono, SSet.S.le_iff and related simplex-order formulas, and boundary generators. These describe faces or ordinary orders, not the cofinality of the opposite injective-simplex category.

mathlib_searches.results: Eight hits concern face operators, truncation inclusions, opposite simplicial sets and representability of faces; none states the required homotopy-cofinality theorem.
